review_notes: I read the whole target file and checked the `kappaSeq` and `kappaAt` definitions. I also searched the project for other proofs of `kappaSeq κ M M = κ` and for places that unfold `kappaSeq` through simp. The file has no `@[simp]` declarations. Its analytic lemmas are conditional inequalities, which are not good simp lemmas. The only simp-interface problem I found is the missing simp lemma for `kappaSeq` at the top level. I did not run Lean, so I have not tested the proposed lemma or the effect of adding it. I did not check whether `KappaSeq.lean` can import everything the lemma needs. That is unlikely to be a problem, since `kappaAt` is already imported there.

findings.excerpt: have hkeq : I.kappaSeq κ j j = κ := by simp [Ingredients.kappaSeq, Ingredients.kappaAt]
findings.problem: `Ingredients.kappaSeq` has no canonical simp lemma for the top level `kappaSeq κ M M = κ`. The definition is `kappaAt κ m (M - m)`. Each proof of the fact has to unfold both `kappaSeq` and `kappaAt` and rely on `Nat.sub_self` and the zero-depth equation. The same proof is repeated in several files: `CaseBig.lean` (`kappaSeq_top`), `SeparatedChainsAssembly.lean` (`NoSel.kappaSeq_top`, a second copy with a different name), and inline `hk` lemmas in `Section5/LeftToShow/Scales.lean`. Many other proofs use `simp [Ingredients.kappaSeq]` to expose `kappaAt κ m (M - m)`, so `kappaSeq` is unfolded ad hoc instead of through a stable simp interface. The two named copies sit in unrelated files, so the fact is not available to the whole project as a simp rule.
findings.proposed_change: In `Statements/Section4/KappaSeq.lean`, right after `def kappaSeq`, add `@[simp] theorem kappaSeq_self (κ : ℝ) (M : ℕ) : I.kappaSeq κ M M = κ` with the proof `by simp [kappaSeq, kappaAt]`. The left side is a strict `kappaSeq` pattern and the right side is a variable, so the rewrite is terminating and non-looping. Optionally also add `kappaSeq_def : I.kappaSeq κ M m = I.kappaAt κ m (M - m) := rfl` as a non-simp unfolding lemma. Then replace the inline `hkeq` here with `simp` or `rw [kappaSeq_self]`. Delete the duplicates `kappaSeq_top` and `NoSel.kappaSeq_top` and the inline `hk` copies in `Section5/LeftToShow/Scales.lean`.
findings.benefit: The top-level normal form `κ_M = κ` is then produced by plain `simp` wherever `kappaSeq κ M M` appears. Callers no longer need `simp [Ingredients.kappaSeq, Ingredients.kappaAt]`, which unfolds the definition completely. The duplicated, separately named lemmas collapse into one.
